step1_analysis.description: A 3rd-order doubly-terminated passive LC ladder low-pass filter. This normalized prototype is typically used as a starting point for synthesizing active OTA-C or Gm-C filters as discussed in the paper.

paper_reference.title: A Field Programmable Analog Array for CMOS Continuous-Time OTA-C Filter Applications

dc_gain.description: Low frequency (DC) gain of the filter

sky130_expected.reasoning: Determined by the resistive voltage divider of the source and load terminations (R1 and R4).

cutoff_freq.description: -3dB cutoff frequency relative to DC gain

sky130_expected.calculation: Normalized prototype with L~2.2H and C~1.1F corresponds to a cutoff of 1 rad/s.

passband_ripple.description: Maximum gain variation in the passband

sky130_expected.calculation: Based on Chebyshev prototype values (g1=2.216, g2=1.088).
sky130_expected.reasoning: The component values match a 3rd-order Chebyshev response with approximately 1.5 dB ripple.

step3_testbench.description: AC analysis to measure the frequency response of the normalized RLC prototype filter.
step3_testbench.spice:
* RLC Filter Prototype Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* DUT Netlist
V0 V0 GND
R1 V0 N1 1
L1 N1 V2 2.2160
C2 V2 GND 1.0883
L3 V2 V4 2.2160
R4 V4 GND 1

.control
* Set V0 as AC source for frequency response analysis
alter V0 ac=1

* Run AC analysis from 0.001 Hz to 10 Hz
ac dec 100 0.001 10

* Calculate gain in dB
let gain_db = vdb(V4)

* Measure DC gain (at very low frequency)
meas ac dc_gain find gain_db at=0.001

* Measure -3dB cutoff frequency
let target_gain = dc_gain - 3
meas ac cutoff_freq when gain_db=target_gain fall=1

* Measure passband ripple
meas ac max_gain max gain_db from=0.001 to=0.15
let passband_ripple = max_gain - dc_gain

print dc_gain cutoff_freq passband_ripple
quit
.endc
.end
